newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia MoF resists long T-bill yield fall.
newsitem.headline: Russia MoF resists long T-bill yield fall.

text.p: The Russian Finance Ministry accepted a yield above market levels at an auction of 364-day GKO discount Treasury bill as it opposes a quick fall in long-term yields which could prompt a bout of profit-taking, dealers said.
The 24.87 percent yield on a 168-day T-bill was in line with the market, where yields averaged 25.20 percent on Tuesday.
But the average yield on the 364-day paper was 26.98 percent.

"At the first (364-day) auction the Finance Ministry could have got a smaller yield -- the volume of demand would have made that possible and almost 80 percent of bids were non-competitive ones," said Alexei Orekhov, Renaissance Capital's vice-president of fixed income.
"But the Finance Ministry understands that it is not good to push the yield down too far, as that could provoke profit-taking and a price fall."

Dealers said foreign investors were unaffected by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision not to change its rate as investment in long-term T-bills give a high hard currency yield as the rouble was rising on the forward market.
Dealers said the absence of a yield premium at the second auction would lead to a price rise at Thursday's trading.

"There remained a significant unsatisfied demand after the auctions and it is clear there will be even more funds," said Alfa-Bank dealer Alexander Inzhiyevsky. "That's why there is a possibility of a price rise within 0.3 percentage points on medium and long-term issues."
